evidence:
Overall the criteria are strongly outcome-based and browser-decidable. The 40 functional binary rows, 5 polish binary rows, 2 gate rows and 5 anchored visual Likert rows each name observable outcomes: stage and order readbacks in an independent context, replayed captured requests with HTTP status, document.activeElement, getBoundingClientRect().top, scroll offsets and response-body inspection. They have positive controls and suffixed per-review probes (functional prompt.md:15 and :21 'unique suffix'; S/M/L/C/B protocols at :35-:43). Colderwater lessons 7 and 14 (timing repeat/void handling) are handled in both timed dimensions. functional prompt.md:21 and polish prompt.md:80 define one browser_run_code_unsafe action, with t0 recorded only after a successful trigger, 500 ms polling and a {triggerOk, met, ms} return. Void means an error before t0 or a failed trigger; at most two repeats are allowed, and a completed met=false is never repeated. Negative watches run the full 15000 ms with a fresh-context reconfirmation. Every within-15-seconds row (hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread) goes through that rule: functional :47 'a timed observation', :49 'Every reading in U ... is a timed observation', :55; polish :76 'Each live row is one timed observation'. Lesson 8: the modifier-hold instruction is present (app_context.md:273-275). Lesson 9: 'Report every step', with a skipped step failing (functional :23-25, polish :82-84, visual :108-110). Lesson 13: no judge prompt has a public internet address; only localhost appears. Lesson 15: hro_restart (judge.toml:412-419) re-reads many records after a real restart_app: jobs, per-stage order, notes, messages, unread counts, activity, and the seeded order and note. Distinctive probes: Noor's seeded messages are uniquely numbered (#001-#120), so the hro_thread_latest/hro_thread_earlier legs ('wrong 30 / missing / repeated / out of order') are decidable. Lena's starting unread of 1 matches the seed reads. hro_stale_refused uses an ABA probe (F Applied->Screen, Mei moves it back, the stale request is replayed) that tells a real version check apart from a from-stage check. K uses a unique-suffix rejection reason searched across every candidate response. Raw evidence index hashes verified; it is scripted golden evidence only, not a configured judge run.

CONFIRMED DEFECT (instance 1, P2): the hro_reopen reason legs have no defined evidence surface. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:103 requires 'after reopening the reason is gone; undoing that reopening puts the card back in Rejected with its reason' and 'Fails if it ... keeps its reason, or loses the reason on undo', but does not say where the reason is read. The sibling hro_reject_reason (judge.toml:85) explicitly allows the reason to be available to staff only 'on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line'. hireops_rules.md:116-117 requires the immutable Activity rejection line to keep its reason ('A rejection line includes its reason ... Nothing in it is ever edited or removed'). Take an app that shows the reason only in Activity, which hro_reject_reason permits. After reopening, 'the reason is gone' cannot be decided in the browser, because the history line still shows it. After an undo, the old history line satisfies 'with its reason' even if the current card lost its reason. The golden shows the reason on the card only while it is REJECTED (solution/app/public/js/board.js:131, :255), so the reference is unaffected; the defect is in the criterion.

Further instances, lower severity, verdict unchanged:
(2, P3) hro_candidate_view (judge.toml:391) 'the wording follows stage changes' and K (prompt.md:51) 'reading Tomas's status wording after each move' do not say whether Tomas's page may be reloaded or re-opened, or must update live. hireops_rules.md section 5 lists board cards, unread counts and messages for live updates but not candidate status wording. A judge reading an already-open candidate page straight away could fail a conforming reload-only candidate view, or pass and fail inconsistently.
(3, P3, note) hro_move_one_stage (judge.toml:58) 'shows the card in its new stage at the first look after the action, without a reload or another person's update' cannot tell an optimistic or immediate update from a short polling refresh, given judge latency. This only weakens the 'straight away' leg (hireops_rules.md:86); it does not fail correct apps. REVIEW_POLICY forbids one-second timing distinctions, so this is accepted as a deliberate trade-off.
(4, P3, note) The third path of hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:139, 'focus is on a control of that card after you looked for the move there') is satisfied by the judge's own click. This is a deliberate leniency for UIs that never move the card, and it does not let a broken app pass the reason or real-place legs.

Runtime: no configured judge run, Oracle grade or model score exists for this candidate (the raw-evidence-index scope says so). Whether the long functional protocol is decidable in a real judge run is unmeasured and remains a risk.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that can fail: an app that, as hro_reject_reason allows, shows a rejection's reason only in the Activity line and the rejected-from stage on the reopen control. In protocol M, after C is reopened to Applied, the judge looks for the reason and finds it still in the Activity rejection line, which hireops_rules.md:117 forbids editing. It fails hro_reopen for 'keeps its reason' even though the card's reason was cleared. Broken app that can pass: an app that shows the reason on the card and in Activity, but drops reject_reason when an undo restores a reopened card to Rejected. The unchanged original Activity line satisfies 'with its reason', so the judge passes the 'loses the reason on undo' leg.
suggested_fix: In hro_reopen and the matching M protocol sentence, state that whether the reason is present is read from the card's current state (the card, its details or its reopen control, or a fresh board or card read the UI makes), never from the Activity history, whose old rejection line keeps the reason by design. Optionally, make hro_candidate_view say Tomas's status may be read after reloading or re-opening his applications list; if live candidate updates are intended, say so in the brief and route the check through the timed-observation rule.
